LESSON: READING 1.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one read widely? 2. How does one identify print and non-print texts that are interesting to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self–efficacy as the learner chooses grade appropriate reading materials and reads independently.

● Learning to learn as the learner gains self-discipline as they work collaboratively to search for extra information online and

from other sources.

Values:
Responsibility: A learner engages and helps each other in groups when selecting the reading

materials.

Link to other subjects:

Social Studies handles human rights as a pertinent issue.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Print texts

• Braille texts

• Dictionary both print and braille

• Electronic reading materials,

• Digital devices with assistive technology
